thought.text: This is the exact RLS policy the production bootstrap applies. Let me replicate it so the worker role can claim jobs.

reasoning_content: Now I understand exactly how the production bootstrap provisions the job-worker RLS policy. Let me replicate that exact policy creation SQL to make the worker role able to claim jobs. This is the documented bootstrap behavior (the same `bootstrap-entrypoint.sh` that runs in CI/swarm). Let me apply it.

action.command:
cd /workspace && docker exec -i sva-studio-postgres psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U sva -d sva_studio <<'SQL'
DO $worker_policies$
DECLARE
  table_record record;
BEGIN
  FOR table_record IN
    SELECT c.relname
    FROM pg_class c
    JOIN pg_namespace n ON c.oid = c.oid
    JOIN pg_namespace n2 ON c.relnamespace = n2.oid
    WHERE n2.nspname = 'graphile_worker'
      AND c.relkind IN ('r', 'p')
      AND c.relrowsecurity = true
  LOOP
    EXECUTE format('DROP POLICY IF EXISTS sva_job_worker_access ON graphile_worker.%I', table_record.relname);
    EXECUTE format('CREATE POLICY sva_job_worker_access ON graphile_worker.%I TO sva_job_worker USING (true) WITH CHECK (true)', table_record.relname);
  END LOOP;
END
$worker_policies$;
SELECT tablename, policyname FROM pg_policies WHERE tablename LIKE '%_private%';
SQL
echo "policy exit=$?"

summary: Create worker RLS policy on graphile tables
